note: Window agent p1880-p1889, 2 Nov 2026. events/0-1 and keyframe_overrides/0 settle the Chile-Peru occupations of the War of the Pacific (Chile holds only Tarapaca as its own land; Tacna and Arica stay Peruvian land under Chilean occupation from the Treaty of Ancon; the Cliopatria shape's Puno, Lima, Ica and Arequipa cells are not Chile's). rulings/0-3: border-fit speckle, Mexico and the British shape holding cells inside the United States and the United States holding cells inside Canada (the borders did not move 1880-1889). rulings/4: Southern Bessarabia is Russian from the Treaty of Berlin, not nobody's land 1880-1884. keyframe_overrides/1-2: the Loango coast (239 cells) that the Loango dossier hands to French Africa in 1883 is kept in French Africa's 1884 and 1885-1889 shapes instead of falling to nobody's land.

region.text: the provinces of Tacna and Arica

events.note: 20 October 1883: the Treaty of Ancon. Peru 'formally cede[s] Tarapaca to Chile', but Chile is 'to occupy the provinces of Tacna and Arica for 10 years' with a plebiscite to follow, so Tacna and Arica stay Peruvian land held by Chile. The October 1883 occupation_end events (Tarapaca, Lima) close the whole Chile-over-Peru relation and returned Tacna and Arica to Peru as free land for 1883-1884; this event re-opens the occupation (Peru sovereign, Chile occupier). Dated November so that it applies after the dossiers' October ends.

region.text: the provinces of Tacna and Arica

events.note: Chile keeps Tacna and Arica under occupation after its last expeditionary forces embark at Callao ('On 4 August 1884, Lynch and the rest of the Chilean Expeditionary Forces embarked in Callao for Chile'), as the Treaty of Ancon (20 October 1883) provided: Chile 'was also to occupy the provinces of Tacna and Arica for 10 years'. Compiler note: the August 1884 occupation_end events (Moquegua, Arequipa, Puno) close the whole Chile-over-Peru relation, so this event re-opens it for Tacna and Arica; dated September so that it applies after the August ends. Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: note reordered so that the map caption (its first sentence) reads as history, not compiler mechanics.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1880-1884 Chile shape without the Peruvian departments other than Tacna and Moquegua (which the occupation events hold): Puno, Lima, Ica and Arequipa were occupied at most, never Chilean land; Tarapaca (a Chilean region today) and Arica stay in the shape

keyframe_overrides.why: The page: Lima was occupied from January 1881 to 29 October 1883, 'The occupation of Arequipa and Puno at the end of the war saw little military action' and only Tarapaca was ceded ('Peru formally cede Tarapaca to Chile'). Cliopatria's shape draws parts of Puno (58 cells), Lima (15), Ica (5) and Arequipa (3) as Chilean direct land for 1880-1884, which made the size rule give Chile those cells; the ledger already carries the occupations (Lima 1881-1883, Moquegua 1880-1884).

union.text: the Loango coast: Kouilou, Pointe-Noire, Niari and Nyanga

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1880 shape plus Tunisia (protectorate of 12 May 1881) plus Guinea (occupied 1884), plus the former Loango coast (Kouilou, Pointe-Noire, Niari, Nyanga), French Congo land from the dissolution of the Kingdom of Loango in 1883

keyframe_overrides.why: The page: French Congo 'was formally established as the French Congo on 30 November 1882' and the claim 'was confirmed at the Berlin Conference of 1884-85'. The Loango dossier hands its coast to French Africa in 1883, but Cliopatria's French shape of 1884 has no Congo coast, so the keyframe snap threw the 239 cells (Niari 106, Nyanga 79, Kouilou 54) back to nobody's land for 1884.

union.text: the Loango coast: Kouilou, Pointe-Noire, Niari and Nyanga

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1885 shape plus the former Loango coast (Kouilou, Pointe-Noire, Niari, Nyanga), which stays French Congo land through 1889

keyframe_overrides.why: Same as french-africa_1884: French Congo, established 30 November 1882 and 'confirmed at the Berlin Conference of 1884-85', holds the Loango coast through the 1880s (Gabon was only 'formally added' in 1891, so Gabon proper is not added). Cliopatria's 1885 shape (1885-1889) lacks it, and the keyframe snap left the 239 cells as nobody's land for 1885-1889.

rulings.why: The page: 'the middle of the Rio Grande was the border' (Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo) and 'Five years later, the Gadsden Purchase completed the creation of the current U.S.-Mexico border'; a second treaty followed in 1884 and nothing moves the line north. The 27 cells Mexico holds in Texas (20), New Mexico (4) and Arizona (3) are border-fit speckle of the shape, not Mexican land.

The page: the Oregon Treaty (1846) 'established the 49th parallel as the boundary through the Rockies', the 1872 arbitration 'established the border between the Gulf Islands and the San Juan Islands', and it describes no border change between 1880 and 1889. The 29 cells the British shape takes from the United States in 1885 are border-fit speckle.
Same border (49th parallel of 1846, 1872 San Juan arbitration, no change 1880-1889): cells inside Canada's borders go to Canada, not to the United States by the size rule.
Same border: cells inside the United States (Alaska, Vermont, Montana and others) go to the United States, not to Canada by the size rule.

region.text: southern Bessarabia's Moldovan districts (Cahul, Cantemir, Taraclia, Comrat)

rulings.why: Signed 13 July 1878: 'Romania was forced to cede southern Bessarabia to the Russian Empire' (Romania received Dobruja in return). The 12-13 Moldovan cells the Russian 1880 shape claims were Romanian at the 1880 anchor, then fell to nobody's land when Romania's 1880 shape dropped them, and reached Russia only in 1884.
